A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraftLLM and modular SkillPacks despite the changed title. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original capability-transfer, model-fusion, compression, forget-free learning and detoxification experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds domain-fusion experiments, router analyses, qualitative cases and comparative resource measurements.

M1.justification: The SFT/DPO transfer pipeline, module-specific delta compression and routed SkillPacks remain. v2 elaborates rank selection, reconstruction and routing; v1 already documents truncated SVD and task/source-based routing in Appendices F.3 and B.3. The concrete compression settings remain identical, so these elaborations do not establish a changed implemented procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds specialist-model fusion across finance, law and biomedicine in Section 5.4 and Table 4, extending evaluation to explicitly divergent domain specializations. Appendix C.3 additionally examines mixed-domain queries. The original general, mathematical, coding, instruction-following and detoxification coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 11 adds Sequential Distillation to the existing code-to-math comparison in v1 Table 9. Its new domain comparison also includes individual LLaMA-7B specialists and an AdaptLLM reference. Existing fusion and detoxification comparator sets remain; reusing FuseChat and Twin-Merging on new domains alone is not a comparator change.

E3.justification: Added experiments use LLaMA-7B domain models with a 10% per-SkillPack parameter budget, compare top-1, top-2 and top-3 activation, and evaluate comparative training, compression and inference costs. The established experiments retain their reported splits, metrics and training budgets. Newly disclosed router-training and calibration settings do not establish revisions to those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds module-wise pruning and rank-sensitivity curves in Figures 5–6, multi-SkillPack interaction tests in Section 6.3, mixed-domain routing cases in Appendix C.3, and comparative resource analysis in Table 18. These substantially extend investigation of compression sensitivity, skill complementarity and deployment costs beyond the retained ablations and hyperparameter studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The statement about multiple response-generation runs using different random seeds remains unchanged in Appendix F.1.

E6.justification: v2 adds domain-fusion scores, top-k routing results, resource measurements and sequential-distillation results. Table 4 reports averages of 49.6 for GraftLLM, 47.3 for FuseChat and 47.9 for Twin-Merging under the new setting. Most original scores remain, but the highest-parameter LoRA DPO point changes from approximately 69.4 to 69.8 (v1 Figure 6; v2 Figure 8). The compressed-code average also changes from 60.9 to 61.3 despite unchanged component scores (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 11).

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit cumulative singular-value-energy condition for MLP rank selection in Equation 5. It also removes v1 Equation 3's inconsistent source–target delta definition, retaining the adapted-target-minus-base definition already present in v1 Section 3.1. These are limited formal refinements; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims of compact transferable SkillPacks, efficient heterogeneous fusion, reduced interference and forgetting resistance. The new title emphasizes fusion, but the principal scientific contributions and claimed application scope remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds spectral-decay reasoning for attention compression and explains why ensembling helps similar tasks more than divergent domains. Its limitations section becomes less explicit: v1's reconstruction-overhead and layer-adaptive MoE restrictions disappear, and the manual-hyperparameter limitation becomes general future work. Dependence on distillation quality remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 fills important implementation gaps by specifying the router architecture, embedding features, batch size, learning rate and training steps in Appendix B.3. It documents compression-parameter selection, identifies C4 validation data for GPTQ calibration, and expands resource accounting. An anonymous code link and explicit release-content statement are also added. These are substantial disclosures rather than evidence that the retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 reframes the discussion around homogeneous versus heterogeneous model fusion, adds TSV-Merge and removes the Delta-DCT discussion. AdaptLLM is newly cited for the domain experiment. The broader positioning relative to distillation, compression and routing methods remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and reorganizes the methodology: the standalone SFT/DPO exposition is removed, while SkillPack compression, reconstruction and routing receive expanded treatment. It also changes the title and terminology, adds appendix navigation and disclosure statements, and switches to author–year citations.

P2.justification: v2 adds two sensitivity figures and four tables covering domains, routing, qualitative cases and resources. Existing performance plots receive new legends, several tables gain shading and highlighting, and tables and figures are redistributed throughout the document. These constitute substantial display changes beyond renumbering or numerical edits.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation of compression and routing, adds a sequential-distillation control, and supplies important router and calibration details missing from v1. These improve scrutiny and reproducibility. Benefits are tempered by sparsely specified domain experiments, less explicit limitations and numerical errors: Table 4's finance-model average is 57.0 although its scores average about 47.0, and Table 11 changes the compressed-code average incorrectly. The additions provide a limited net improvement without overturning the retained main comparisons.
